basic_info.one_liner: Thai gold investors who buy a fixed amount on a regular schedule (monthly baht-cost averaging into 96.5% gold bars or digital gold savings/funds), hold for years, and measure success by average cost, total return versus cash savings, and the discipline to keep buying through corrections.

needs.jobs_to_be_done: Accumulate wealth in gold in small, disciplined steps without needing to time the market; protect savings from inflation and the feeling that cash 'won't stay saved' (a common Thai motivation: 'เก็บเงินไม่อยู่ต้องออมทอง' - if you can't save cash, save gold). They need to always know where they stand versus their own average cost and versus simply keeping the money in a bank deposit; to get steady, calm guidance on whether to keep buying or pause when price corrects; to convert digital savings into physical bars/coins when ready (gold as a trusted, tangible asset and a way to pass wealth to family - Thai demand is #1 in ASEAN, top-10 globally per YLG); and to avoid the leverage/futures traps that cause most gold-investor losses (per MTS Gold's chairman: a 10% margin + 2% price drop = 20% loss).
needs.top_questions: 1) 'Am I in profit or loss right now versus my average cost - in baht, not just percent?' 2) 'Gold keeps falling - should I keep buying every month or pause first?' (the classic saver's dilemma 'should I buy the dip or wait?', echoed across Thai gold media during the 2026 correction) 3) 'If I save 1,000-3,000 baht every month, how many grams / how many bars will I have in 5 years?' 4) 'Why did the gold price drop today - should I worry?' 5) 'Can I withdraw my app savings as real gold bars, and what are the fees/spreads?' 6) 'If I sell today, how much cash do I actually get after the shop spread?' 7) 'What share of my portfolio should be gold?' (common guidance: cap around 10%) 8) 'App gold savings vs gold mutual fund vs physical bars at the shop - which is better for me and what do they cost?'
needs.decision_drivers: Distance of current price from their own average cost; belief in the long-term uptrend narrative (central-bank buying streaks, '$4,000 is the new base' story from big Thai gold houses); comparison of gold's total return versus fixed deposits and cash savings; visible fees, spreads and conversion costs; whether the platform lets them take physical gold (trust anchor for Thai savers); liquidity for emergencies; regulatory news (Bank of Thailand curbs on online gold trading cut volumes ~60% in 2026, possible trading tax); and explicit warnings that leveraged products (futures/margin) are the real loss-maker, so they stay with physical/DCA products.

pains.top_pains: Holding losses after buying near the peak ('stuck on the mountain' - ติดดอย): in 2026 Thai gold funds returned about -30% in H1 and baht gold fell from over 70,000 to ~64,000 baht/baht-weight, so many regular buyers are under water. The agonizing keep-buying-or-pause decision during corrections with no tool showing the math on THEIR plan. Opaque real returns: shop buy/sell spreads, premiums, fund fees and conversion fees are scattered and rarely netted out. Price whiplash anxiety - local prices are revised up to 15 times a day. Conflicting guru forecasts (70,000 is the new base / 100,000-baht gold someday vs asset managers telling people to cut gold after a -30% half) leave them whipsawed. Fear of scam or unlicensed platforms, and uncertainty about Bank of Thailand rules and possible taxes.
pains.confusion_points: Units: baht-weight (15.16g) vs gram vs troy ounce. Purity: 96.5% local bars vs 99.99% app/fund gold - average costs cannot be compared naively. Local price vs world price (baht exchange rate makes Thai gold move differently). Buy/sell spread and why selling back gives less than the board price. Difference between gold savings in an app, gold mutual funds, and physical bars (fees, tax, redemption), and especially 'gold fund' vs 'gold mining equity fund' (in 2025 they returned +61.95% vs +141.23% - completely different risk). Why gold falls when everything looks bad (Fed rate HIKES on oil-driven inflation in 2026, opportunity cost). Jargon: DCA, support/resistance, realized vs unrealized loss.
pains.trust_barriers: Scam fear and doubts about whether 'digital gold' is really vaulted gold - the single strongest trust move in the Thai market in 2026 was apps adding physical withdrawal (KKP Dime partnered MTS/YLG so 100-baht savers can convert to real bars/coins from 0.05 troy oz). Black-box AI advice ('sell now' with no reason) - users distrust predictions without cited evidence, especially when famous analysts contradict each other. Unfamiliar platforms versus century-old gold shops (MTS, YLG, Hua Seng Heng carry inherited trust). Concerns about where analysis data comes from, and about regulatory standing (BOT measures, potential tax) - people fear platforms that could be shut down or taxed.

ux.must_have_first_screen: Within 5 seconds: (1) current portfolio value in THB and total P/L versus average cost in BOTH baht and percent; (2) today's buy/sell prices (with the shop spread visible, e.g. bar sell-out price); (3) the user's average cost per baht-weight next to today's price; (4) next scheduled DCA buy (date + amount) with a pause/skip affordance; (5) one plain-Thai line: why gold moved today, with source chips; (6) a price chart with the user's average-cost line drawn on it. Agent activity should be visible but secondary - a compact 'analysts are reviewing your plan' indicator, not a wall of text.
ux.workflow_preferences: Mobile-first single page (the growth of Thai gold accumulation is happening on phones: KKP Dime 267k users, +95% volume in a year; apps let savers start at 100 baht, pick the day and amount, and adjust anytime). Rhythm matters more than features: a quick daily glance at P/L; the real session is monthly around payday/auto-buy day (review plan, confirm or adjust the next buy); a yearly review of total return vs cash. Push notifications only on meaningful events: price crossing their average cost, a >3-5% daily move, monthly buy reminder, physical-gold threshold reached. Progressive disclosure: one-tap expansion from any number into the agents' reasoning with citations. Must support manually logging offline purchases from gold shops, since many accumulators mix shop bars with app savings.
ux.language_and_tone: Plain everyday Thai, warm and reassuring (gold is a 'comfort asset' - the KKP Dime product team explicitly says UX must make buy > check savings > withdraw physical feel seamless, clear and uncomplicated). Prefer Thai terms over English jargon: say 'ทยอยซื้อทุกเดือน / ออมทองรายเดือน' for DCA, explain anything technical in tap-to-explain chips. Numbers in Thai formats: '64,000 บาท/บาททอง', Buddhist calendar years (พ.ศ. 2569), every percentage paired with its baht amount ('-12% (-9,400 บาท)'). Short sentences; details expand on demand; never moralize about losses.
ux.accessibility_notes: [uncertain - inferred, not directly verified by sources] Adjustable font size (16sp+ body, large-number mode for key figures), WCAG AA contrast, color-blind-safe gain/loss encoding (green/red PLUS ▲▼ arrows and +/- signs - never color alone), one-hand-reach bottom action bar, reduce-motion option, and high-contrast large numerals for the 40+ cohort that also accumulates gold.

design.implications_for_gold_assistant: 1) AVERAGE-COST LINE ON THE CHART: overlay a dashed horizontal line at the user's weighted average cost with a floating label ('average cost 62,400 / today 64,000 = +2.6% (+8,200 THB)'); shade the gap between price and cost line; default ranges 1Y/5Y/MAX with intraday collapsed behind an explicit 'daily' toggle so long-horizon framing wins. 2) 'AM I WINNING?' HEADER CARD: total value, P/L vs average cost in baht AND %, average cost per baht-weight and per gram, today's sell-back price net of spread ('if you sold all today you'd get X baht'); recompute on price change but throttle refreshes to avoid 15x/day anxiety. 3) DCA PLAN CARD: next auto-buy (date, amount), 12-month progress bar and accumulation streak, total grams accumulated, goal marker (e.g. '1 baht-weight bar'), with actions: change amount / skip this month / pause for 1-3 months (pause, never hard-cancel) - mirrors what Thai gold apps ship (choose day, choose amount, adjust anytime, withdraw real gold). 4) 'KEEP BUYING OR PAUSE?' DECISION SUPPORT: when spot < average cost or price fell >=5% in 30 days, surface a card with three options (continue / reduce amount / pause) and compute - on the user's own plan - the resulting new average cost and total grams for each under a 12-month scenario, plus the Quant agent's evidence chips (e.g. how DCA buyers fared through past deep corrections, citing published deep-correction statistics from YLG) and a Risk agent note; frame as options with reasons, never as a command, and never push stop-loss selling at this segment. 5) 'VS CASH' COMPARISON STRIP: total return of their actual monthly contributions versus (a) the same contributions in a fixed deposit and (b) one lump sum on their first purchase date - accumulators judge gold against cash savings, so show 'if this had been a deposit: ~X baht'. 6) UNIFIED MULTI-PRODUCT LEDGER: consolidate shop bars (96.5%), app gold savings (99.99%) and gold funds into one list with per-product average cost, all normalized to grams and THB, purity badge on every row, and a per-row 'fees + spread paid so far' figure; allow manual entry for offline shop purchases. 7) PHYSICAL CONVERSION TRACKER: show progress toward the physical-withdrawal minimum (e.g. 0.05 troy oz), a transparent conversion calculator (spread + casting/withdrawal fee + delivery insurance) BEFORE confirmation, and partner-shop trust badges with pickup or insured-mail options. 8) AGENTS' DIVISION OF LABOR FOR THIS SEGMENT: News/Macro agents answer 'why did gold fall today' in 2-3 plain-Thai sentences with linked sources; Quant agent runs the DCA scenario math; Risk agent explicitly separates gold-price risk from leverage risk and the app must never show futures/margin promotions or CTAs to these users (leverage is where Thai gold investors actually lose money per MTS Gold); Lead Researcher delivers a monthly plain-Thai summary email/push: 'this month you bought X g at avg Y; your average cost moved from A to B'. 9) TRUST SURFACES: every agent claim carries citation chips into the knowledge graph; show regulatory/licence status and physical-gold proof; tone guidelines ban guaranteed-return language.
design.antipatterns_to_avoid: Intraday-first ticker dashboards and flashing red/green tiles (prices revise up to 15 times a day; it manufactures anxiety for people who buy monthly). Push notifications urging timing moves, 'hot tips', or leveraged products. Showing only percentages without baht amounts. Black-box 'AI says: sell' verdicts without reasons, sources, or confidence - this kills trust fastest. One-sided bullish hype (Thai users see contradictory guru forecasts daily; overconfidence reads as scam). Hiding spreads/fees/redemption costs until checkout. Separate product silos with incompatible units (96.5% bars vs 99.99% app gold) and no normalization. Confusing 'gold fund' with 'gold mining fund' labels. Gamified streak guilt-tripping when a user must pause a month. Any aesthetic that resembles known Thai investment scams: guaranteed returns, countdown pressure, unsolicited DMs.
